n: After the September 1830 conference, the Lord gently rebukes David Whitmer for fearing man more than relying on God for strength. David had been among those influenced by Hiram Page’s stone.
David focused more on earthly things than on God and his ministry, ignored the Spirit and his leaders, and followed people God hadn’t appointed.

f.w: persuaded by those whom I have not commanded

n: So David must seek answers from God himself and ponder what he has already received.

f.w: ponder upon the things which you have received

n: David should stay at his father’s house and serve in the Church and the surrounding area until further instruction.
Peter Whitmer Jr. is called to accompany Oliver on the mission to the Lamanites, to fearlessly declare the gospel and follow Oliver’s counsel.

f.w: take your journey with your brother Oliver

n: Peter should share Oliver’s hardships and pray for both their deliverance, since Oliver has power to build up the Church among the Lamanites.
Only Joseph Smith presides over Oliver in Church matters — reinforcing the order taught in D&C 28.

f.w: except it is his brother, Joseph Smith, Jun.

n: Diligent obedience will bring Peter eternal life.
John Whitmer is called to begin preaching boldly, like a trumpet.

f.w: as with the voice of a trump

n: His labor will be at Philip Burroughs’s home and surrounding area — a neighbor in Seneca County, New York — wherever he can be heard.

f.g: a neighbor of the Whitmers near Fayette, whose home was used for preaching.

n: John’s entire work from now on is for Zion. He should speak without fearing people, for the Lord is with him.

f.w: not fearing what man can do
